font.$description: Layer 1 typography. The scale is named by pixel size, like the spacing and radius scales, so a step is never confused with a weight or a level of hierarchy. Font families are not here: they are injected at runtime by next/font and are declared in app/globals.css, which is the only place that knows their generated variable names.

size.$description: Ten steps, in px. 15 is body copy in the UI, 16 is the document pane, 13 is a dense control, 10 and 12 are labels. The gaps widen as the scale climbs because a difference that reads as deliberate at 12px is invisible at 32px.

tracking.$description: Letter spacing per size step. Normal below 16px, then tightening as the size climbs to roughly -0.022em at display sizes. Large type set at normal tracking reads loose and amateur; small type set tight reads muddy, which is why this is a curve rather than one value.

leading.$description: Line height per size step, unitless. Loosens for reading sizes and tightens for headings, on the usual principle that a long measure needs more room between lines than a two-word title does.

weight.$description: Three weights, and 700 is deliberately not one of them. On a dense dark interface 600 already reads as emphatic, and 700 reads as shouting; it also costs a font file. Emphasis that 600 cannot carry is a job for size, color or space, not for more weight.
